answer_text:
Let

\[
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle xy^2,\;x^2y,\;z^3\rangle
\]

so that the line integral is

\[
\oint_C \mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r
=
\oint_C xy^2\,dx+x^2y\,dy+z^3\,dz.
\]

By Stokes’ theorem,

\[
\oint_C \mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r
=
\iint_S (\nabla\times \mathbf F)\cdot \mathbf n\,dS,
\]

where \(S\) is any oriented surface with boundary \(C\).

Choose \(S\) to be the portion of the plane

\[
x+y+z=1
\]

inside the cylinder \(x^2+y^2=4\). Since \(C\) is oriented counterclockwise when viewed from above, we choose the upward-pointing normal, i.e. the normal with positive \(z\)-component.

Now compute the curl of \(\mathbf F\):

\[
\nabla\times \mathbf F
=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k\\
\frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\
xy^2 & x^2y & z^3
\end{vmatrix}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\nabla\times \mathbf F
=
\left\langle
\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(z^3)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(x^2y),
\;
\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(xy^2)-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(z^3),
\;
\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^2y)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(xy^2)
\right\rangle.
\]

Compute each component:

\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(z^3)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(x^2y)=0-0=0,
\]

\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(xy^2)-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(z^3)=0-0=0,
\]

\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^2y)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(xy^2)
=2xy-2xy=0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\nabla\times \mathbf F=\langle 0,0,0\rangle.
\]

Hence,

\[
\iint_S (\nabla\times \mathbf F)\cdot \mathbf n\,dS
=
\iint_S \mathbf 0\cdot \mathbf n\,dS
=0.
\]

So by Stokes’ theorem,

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
